newsitem.title: USA: ASARCO forecasts zinc deficit in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: ASARCO forecasts zinc deficit in 1997/98.

text.p: ASARCO, the U.S. base metals producer, said the zinc market will remain in substantial deficit over the next two years, putting upward pressure on prices and tipping the LME contract into backwardation.

ASARCO's chairman, president and chief executive officer Richard de J Osborne forecast at an analysts briefing that the Western world zinc market will see a deficit of 256,000 tonnes this year, and a further deficit of 326,000 tonnes in 1998, compared to a shortfall of 272,000 tonnes last year.
"As stocks come down, we will go into a backwardation," Osborne later told reporters.
Last year ASARCO produced 77,972 tonnes of zinc.
Western world zinc consumption was set to rise 3.5 percent this year and in 1998, while supply was forecast to rise 3.8 percent in 1997 and the following year, Osborne said.
"In 1997 and 1998 the increase in consumption will absorb all the increase in supply," Osborne said.
Zinc stocks were set to fall 582,000 tonnes over the next two years to 4.3 weeks by the end of 1998 from 8.7 weeks at present.
"We could well see continued upward adjustment in the price of zinc," Osborne said.
Fundamentals justified the increased interest in zinc by the funds, speculators and other investors, he added.
Deals such as Pasminco Limited's plan to buy the Century mine from RTZ and CRA would never have happened two or three years ago, Osborne said.
ASARCO has regularly made losses in its lead and zinc operations, but the rebound in the latter's price may alter this trend.
"Zinc may once again be a positive contributor to ASARCO," Osborne said.
In 1996 ASARCO's lead and zinc operations lost $10.6 million, following a loss of $9.6 million in the previous year.
